scenarios.title: Keep maintenance state separate from startup policy
scenarios.objective: Kiln is entering a maintenance window. Change current availability and future enrollment independently. Keep kiln-app.service stopped during maintenance, but enroll it in kiln.target for the next session. Run kiln-inspection.service at virtual port 9200 now, but remove its startup link so it stays stopped next session. Keep kiln-observer.service running at 9100 now and next session. Preserve all supplied files, other links and the default target.

unit_manager_teaching.prerequisite_note: Builds on opening and reading supplied files. The concepts below introduce service status, targets and startup enrollment before you use them. Every command stays inside the virtual manager.

concepts.title: Two independent questions
concepts.text: A service is a program controlled by a service manager. Active asks whether a service is running now. Enabled asks whether startup links request it later. Starting does not enable; enabling does not start. A stopped service can be enabled, and a running one can be disabled.

concepts.title: Read evidence before applying policy
concepts.text: In the worked sketchplan system, use systemctl status sketchplan-app.service and systemctl is-enabled sketchplan-app.service. Read the result, not just a success line from an earlier command. systemctl cat sketchplan-app.service shows the saved WantedBy target. Virtual ports are labels; nothing listens on this computer.

concepts.title: A maintenance plan
concepts.text: The worked plan keeps sketchplan-app.service stopped now but enabled for next time, while sketchplan-inspection.service runs only now. Stop the app and enable it. Start inspection, then disable its startup enrollment. A Check also starts a separate copy from the saved default; it does not change the current practice system.

unit_manager_teaching.example_description: Work in the separate sketchplan system. Keep the app stopped but enabled for later; run inspection only now and preserve the observer.

example_actions.title: Stop sketchplan-app.service
example_actions.explanation: Stop the app for current maintenance; its startup links remain.

example_actions.title: Enable sketchplan-app.service
example_actions.explanation: Enroll the stopped app in its saved WantedBy target; it stays stopped now.

example_actions.title: Start sketchplan-inspection.service
example_actions.explanation: Start the inspection program now; inspect its actual status.

example_actions.title: AdvancePrograms
example_actions.explanation: The simulator finishes bounded program initialization; the terminal start command does this automatically.

example_actions.title: Disable sketchplan-inspection.service
example_actions.explanation: Remove future inspection enrollment without stopping its current program.

unit_manager_teaching.try_change: After the example passes, run systemctl disable sketchplan-app.service. Its current status does not change, but next-session application coverage fails. Enable it again and recheck.

hints: Compare current service status with startup enrollment; changing one need not change the other.
Inspect the selected next target and the failed current/next-session rows. Preserve the named observer and files.

scenarios.explanation: Start/Stop affect current programs. Enable/Disable affect installation links. Set-default chooses the next target; it does not switch the current session. The grader derives a separate next session from the saved policy and checks actual started units, current inputs and preservation. Equivalent supported action orders and harmless comments in editable text are accepted.

scenarios.title: Choose the next target without switching the current session
scenarios.objective: The host is currently in a maintenance session, but the next start must use its normal service group. Select harbor.target for the next session; it must start only that target, harbor-app.service at 8443 and harbor-observer.service at 9100. Keep the current harbor-maintenance.target, harbor-app.service, harbor-inspection.service at 9200 and harbor-observer.service at 9100 active. Do not start harbor.target now. Remove harbor-inspection.service from harbor-maintenance.target startup enrollment. Preserve every file and every other install link.

unit_manager_teaching.prerequisite_note: Builds on opening and reading supplied files. The concepts below introduce service status, targets and startup enrollment before you use them. Every command stays inside the virtual manager.

concepts.title: A target groups services
concepts.text: A target is a named group requested by the manager. Enabling a service adds a link to the target named by WantedBy. A link in one target does not make a different default target request that service.

concepts.title: Next time is different from now
concepts.text: Use systemctl get-default in the worked galleryplan system. systemctl set-default galleryplan.target changes the next-session choice; it does not stop galleryplan-maintenance.target, start the new target or change current services. This is not systemctl isolate, which is outside this simulator.

concepts.title: Observe both sessions
concepts.text: The worked policy keeps current inspection running, removes its maintenance startup link and selects galleryplan.target for next time. Check inspects a separate next-session copy. Current maintenance remains active while the copy starts only the normal target, application and observer.

unit_manager_teaching.example_description: Work in the separate galleryplan system. Select the normal target for later while preserving the current maintenance session.

example_actions.title: Disable galleryplan-inspection.service
example_actions.explanation: Remove only future inspection enrollment; its current program must stay running.

example_actions.title: SetDefault galleryplan.target
example_actions.explanation: Choose the normal target for the next session without starting it now.

unit_manager_teaching.try_change: After the example passes, run systemctl set-default galleryplan-maintenance.target. Current services stay unchanged but next-session results fail. Restore galleryplan.target with set-default and check again.

hints: Compare current service status with startup enrollment; changing one need not change the other.
Inspect the selected next target and the failed current/next-session rows. Preserve the named observer and files.

scenarios.title: Move startup enrollment without leaving an old target link
scenarios.objective: The application is enrolled in the wrong service group. Repair its installation metadata and actual enrollment; editing WantedBy alone does not move existing links. Enroll press-app.service in press.target, remove its old press-maintenance.target link and select press.target for next time. Keep press-app.service running at 8443 using its current saved and loaded definition. Keep press-inspection.service running at 9200 now but absent next session. Keep press-observer.service running at 9100 now and next time. Preserve every application configuration, other unit documents and all other install links. The next session must start only press.target, press-app.service and press-observer.service.

unit_manager_teaching.prerequisite_note: Builds on opening and reading supplied files. The concepts below introduce service status, targets and startup enrollment before you use them. Every command stays inside the virtual manager.

concepts.title: Instructions and installed links differ
concepts.text: WantedBy in [Install] tells Enable where to create a startup link. It is not itself an active dependency. Changing that text and reloading the manager do not remove links created earlier. Inspect the saved text and actual enrollment separately.

concepts.title: Move an enrollment deliberately
concepts.text: In the different proofplan system, disable proofplan-app.service to remove its old enrollment. In the editor change its WantedBy to proofplan.target, Save, and run systemctl daemon-reload. Enable creates the new link. Select proofplan.target as the next default. Other service links must remain untouched.

concepts.title: Loaded and running versions
concepts.text: This task also requires the app’s current run to use the edited source. Reload reads saved definitions but does not replace a running program. Stop and start only proofplan-app.service, then inspect status and the loaded/current inputs. All configuration values stay unchanged. Check independently verifies current work and the next-session group.

unit_manager_teaching.example_description: Work in the separate proofplan system. Move the app from its maintenance enrollment into the normal target and verify its current source.

example_actions.title: Disable proofplan-app.service
example_actions.explanation: Remove old enrollment before creating the replacement.

example_actions.title: Save the app install target
example_actions.explanation: Change only the app’s WantedBy target, preserving application configuration and other unit text.

example_actions.title: DaemonReload
example_actions.explanation: Read saved definitions; this does not restart the current program.

example_actions.title: Enable proofplan-app.service
example_actions.explanation: Create the app’s link in the new target.

example_actions.title: SetDefault proofplan.target
example_actions.explanation: Select the new target for the separate next-session check.

example_actions.title: Stop proofplan-app.service
example_actions.explanation: Stop the old app execution only.

example_actions.title: Start proofplan-app.service
example_actions.explanation: Start the app with the loaded definition and its unchanged application inputs.

example_actions.title: AdvancePrograms
example_actions.explanation: The simulator completes initialization; terminal Start already includes this bounded step.

unit_manager_teaching.try_change: After the example passes, run systemctl disable proofplan-app.service. Its current status does not change, but next-session application coverage fails. Enable it again and recheck.
